cities.name: Bodh Gaya
cities.overview: The town where the Buddha attained enlightenment, and one of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites, with monasteries built by many Buddhist nations.

cities.name: Nalanda
cities.overview: The village of Bargaon in Nalanda district, beside the ruins of the ancient university, about 15 km from Rajgir.

cities.name: Patna
cities.overview: Bihar's capital on the south bank of the Ganga, built on the site of ancient Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan empire.
cities.history: As Pataliputra, it was the capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires and one of the largest cities of the ancient world. It later became the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh.

cities.name: Rajgir
cities.overview: An old capital of Magadha ringed by hills, close to Nalanda, with hot springs and Buddhist and Jain sites.

cities.name: Vaishali
cities.overview: An ancient city north of Patna, an early republic where the Buddha preached his last sermon.

cities.name: Sasaram
cities.overview: A town on the Grand Trunk Road, home to Sher Shah Suri's tomb.

cities.name: Bettiah
cities.overview: The main town in the north-west of Bihar, near Valmiki Tiger Reserve.

cities.name: Begusarai
cities.overview: A town on the Ganges, close to Kanwar Lake.

cities.name: Bhagalpur
cities.overview: A silk city on the Ganges, known for its Tussar silk and the Vikramashila ruins.

cities.name: Gaya
cities.overview: An old pilgrim city on the Phalgu River, where Hindus perform rites for their ancestors.

places.name: Mahabodhi Temple
places.shortDescription: UNESCO-listed temple complex marking the spot where the Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree.
places.description: The Mahabodhi Temple Complex surrounds the place where Siddhartha Gautama meditated and became the Buddha. Its 55 m pyramidal tower rises above a shrine with a gilded Buddha image, and behind it grows a descendant of the original Bodhi tree beside the Vajrasana, the diamond throne. Monks and pilgrims from across Asia chant and meditate in the gardens. Phones are not allowed inside; there is a fee to carry a camera.
places.history: The emperor Ashoka built the first shrine here in the 3rd century BCE. The present temple dates largely from the 5th–6th centuries CE and is one of the earliest brick temples still standing in India. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. December–January is peak season for international pilgrims.

entryFee.note: Free entry; small fee for cameras. Phones must be deposited.

sources.title: Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya – UNESCO

places.name: Nalanda Mahavihara
places.shortDescription: Ruins of one of the world's oldest universities, a great centre of Buddhist learning for some 800 years.
places.description: The excavated ruins of Nalanda spread across red-brick monasteries and temples, with lecture halls, dormitory cells, wells and kitchens laid out in neat rows. The towering Sariputta Stupa, built up in layers over centuries, is the centrepiece. The site museum across the road holds bronzes and sculptures found here, and the modern Xuanzang Memorial Hall remembers the Chinese pilgrim who studied at Nalanda. Hire a guide at the gate to bring the ruins to life.
places.history: Nalanda flourished from the 5th century CE under the Guptas and later the Palas, drawing scholars from across Asia. It was sacked around 1200 CE. The ruins were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Summers are very hot on the open site.

entryFee.note: ASI World Heritage rates (slightly less online); verify before your visit.

sources.title: Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara – UNESCO

places.name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
places.shortDescription: The birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh and one of the five Takhts, the highest seats of Sikh authority.
places.description: Takht Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib stands in the old city of Patna on the site where the tenth Sikh Guru, Gobind Singh, was born. The white marble gurdwara displays relics associated with the Guru, including weapons and a cradle. As at every gurdwara, all visitors are welcome, heads must be covered and shoes removed, and the community kitchen serves free meals. The Guru's birth anniversary (Prakash Parv) brings large celebrations, usually in December or January.
places.history: Guru Gobind Singh was born here in 1666. The present building was rebuilt after an earthquake in 1934, replacing an earlier structure associated with Maharaja Ranjit Singh's patronage.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Prakash Parv of Guru Gobind Singh is the busiest and most festive time.

location.address: Harmandir Gali, Patna City, Patna, Bihar 800008

places.name: Golghar
places.shortDescription: A huge dome-shaped British granary in Patna from 1786, with spiral stairs to the top.
places.description: A giant whitewashed beehive built after a famine, never fully used. Climb the 145 steps for a view of the Ganges.
places.history: Built in 1786 after the great famine of 1770.

images.credit: कवि कलाकार हिमांशु मान्ने (Poet artist himanshu manne)

places.name: Patna Museum
places.shortDescription: Bihar's state museum, founded in 1917, known for its Didarganj Yakshi and Mauryan sculpture.
places.description: An Indo-Saracenic building with a huge fossil tree and bronze Buddhas. Much of the finest material has moved to the new Bihar Museum.

places.name: Great Buddha Statue
places.shortDescription: A giant seated Buddha in stone at Bodh Gaya, one of the largest in India, consecrated in 1989.
places.description: An 80-foot sandstone statue with ten smaller disciples beside it, a short walk from the Mahabodhi Temple. Monasteries from many countries are nearby.
places.history: Consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 1989.

images.credit: Andrew Moore from Johannesburg, South Africa

places.name: Vishwa Shanti Stupa, Rajgir
places.shortDescription: A white peace pagoda on Ratnagiri Hill at Rajgir, reached by a single-seat ropeway.
places.description: An old ropeway swings up to the marble stupa, with its golden Buddhas. Nearby is Griddhakuta, where the Buddha preached.

places.name: Pawapuri
places.shortDescription: The Jain holy site where Mahavira is said to have attained nirvana, with a marble temple in a lake.
places.description: Jal Mandir stands white in a lotus lake, reached by a long causeway. It's about 19 km from Rajgir and among the holiest Jain sites.

places.name: Vaishali Ruins
places.shortDescription: An ancient city and early republic where the Buddha gave his last sermon, with an Ashokan pillar.
places.description: A lion-topped Ashokan pillar stands close to the Coronation Tank, with a peace pagoda and a small museum. The Buddha visited here several times.
places.history: Birthplace of Mahavira, according to tradition.

places.name: Kesariya Stupa
places.shortDescription: A huge excavated Buddhist stupa in East Champaran, among the largest in India.
places.description: A massive brick mound with terraces and niches, 110 km from Patna, that's rarely visited.

places.name: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri
places.shortDescription: A red sandstone tomb on an island in a lake at Sasaram, for the emperor who defeated Humayun.
places.description: A huge, domed octagonal tomb in the middle of a square lake. It's among the finest Afghan buildings in India.
places.history: Built for Sher Shah Suri, founder of the Sur Empire, who died in 1545.

sources.title: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri – Wikipedia

images.alt: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri, Sasaram

places.name: Valmiki National Park
places.shortDescription: Bihar's only national park and tiger reserve, on the Nepal border in West Champaran.
places.description: Sal forest and river flats where the Gandak enters India. It's rarely crowded, and it sits next to Chitwan in Nepal.

places.name: Kanwar Lake
places.shortDescription: Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake, in Begusarai district, an important bird sanctuary.
places.description: A huge wetland that's visited by many winter migrants. Its water level changes a lot, so check first.

places.name: Vikramashila
places.shortDescription: The ruins of a great Buddhist university founded by King Dharmapala, near Bhagalpur.
places.description: Quiet brick ruins of a monastic university that once rivalled Nalanda, with a big central stupa. Few people visit.
places.history: Founded by the Pala king Dharmapala in the 8th century.

places.name: Vishnupad Temple
places.shortDescription: A Vishnu temple on the Phalgu River at Gaya, built around a footprint carved into basalt.
places.description: Hindus come here to perform pind daan for their ancestors, a tradition that peaks during the Pitru Paksha fair.
places.history: The present temple is said to have been rebuilt by Ahilyabai Holkar in the 18th century.
